steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Touriga Nacional probably originated in the Dão and must be at least 20% of the region's red blends. Jaen, the same as Spain's Mencía, gives soft, fruity, floral wines. Alfrocheiro gives colour and red fruit. Tinta Roriz, Tempranillo, adds structure. Dão reds are fresh, floral and structured, with red fruit, pine and spice.

steps.title: Blends
steps.body: Traditionally, Dão wines are blends, often from old field blend vineyards. Touriga Nacional gives aroma and structure; Jaen softness; Alfrocheiro colour; Tinta Roriz body. Single-varietal Touriga Nacional and Jaen are also common now.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.

steps.body: Jaen is the same grape as Mencía, grown across the border in Spain's Bierzo and Ribeira Sacra.

steps.prompt: Which grape is Jaen the same as?
steps.explanation: Jaen and Mencía are the same grape.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Touriga Nacional probably originated in the Dão
Jaen, Alfrocheiro and Tinta Roriz complete the reds
Dão reds are fresh, floral and structured
